directive: Zero-subscription local git log to polished HTML release-notes & customer changelog generator ($9 one-time).

candidates.title: ChangelogKit — Zero-Subscription Git to HTML Release Notes Generator
candidates.buyer_persona: Indie hackers, solo SaaS builders, and open-source maintainers
candidates.recurring_pain: Skipping customer release notes because manual writing is tedious and hosted changelog widgets (Canny $79-$99/mo, Beamer $49-$119/mo) charge recurring subscriptions.
candidates.current_workaround: Leaving GitHub commits raw or manually editing a messy README
candidates.urgency_signal: Users think the product is abandoned when no public changelog exists

evidence.verbatim_quote: Writing changelogs is tedious and usually skipped. I built changelogai.to: connect your GitHub account, select a repo, and AI generates customer-friendly changelogs directly from your commit history.
Well, to be fair writing documentation is tedious (as are changelogs, and writing code).
I'm building a changelog system at the moment. It's basically the github_changelog_generator gem, but without overwriting old changelog entries.

competitors.name: Canny
competitors.main_gap: Expensive per-tracked-user SaaS pricing for solo founders.

competitors.name: Beamer
competitors.main_gap: MAU-metered recurring subscription and paid branding removal.

competitors.name: LaunchNotes
competitors.main_gap: Enterprise product-ops pricing unreachable for indie builders.

market_roi_analyst_rounds.top_distribution_risk: Devs have free CLI tools like git-cliff; positioning focuses on instant zero-config static dark-mode HTML release pages ready for GitHub Pages.

mvp_builder_rounds.test_command: {python} changelog_kit.py --self-test && {python} changelog_kit.py --repo ../.. --name 'Neon Agent House' --md CHANGELOG.md --html changelog.html
